title: A vertex of the asymmetric subtour elimination polytope on eight nodes that is adjacent to no tour
exact_endpoint: ASEP.arc_neighborhood_tour_conjecture_false : ¬ ArcNeighborhoodTourConjecture (arc space R^{n(n-1)}); ASEP.arc_counterexample; matrix-form ASEP.neighborhood_tour_conjecture_false, ASEP.counterexample; ASEP.segment_not_face, ASEP.segment_not_exposed
scope: Vercesi-Barta-Gambardella-Gualandi-Mastrolilli (arXiv:2506.10671) Conjecture 1 states that every vertex of P_ASEP^n has a tour in its neighbourhood. The fractional vertex x*=X/4 of P_ASEP^8 (19 support arcs, 8 tight cuts, rank 56) is adjacent to none of the 5040 tours: for each tour an integer direction certificate shows that [x*,T] is not a face. The conjecture fails at n=8; n=6,7 remain open.
substantive_reason: First refutation of a conjecture stated verbatim in a 2025 polyhedral TSP paper; it also defeats the paper's proposed route to the full V-description by pivoting from an integer vertex. Comparable in kind to the Deza-Indik refutation of the Laurent-Poljak metric-polytope conjecture, which is cited as precedent.
